methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $500M last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Pano AI is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Sonia Kastner and Arvind Satyam, having raised $89M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy) with one public comparable (LNZA), alongside a broader universe of 8 private climate-tech firms including Helion and Redwood Materials.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the company's last post-money valuation of $500M as a base, applying a typical Series B advancement multiplier of 1.9x, yielding $950M. Peer-median analysis across the three comparable firms—valued between $700M and $3.0B—produces a median valuation of $1.0B. The peer set exhibits material dispersion; KoBold Metals trades at $3.0B while Amogy is valued at $700M, reflecting differences in technology maturity and capital intensity across the subsector.

Triangulation of both methods supports a valuation range of $808M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $975M. This relatively tight band reflects reasonable alignment between stage-progression and peer comparables. Key uncertainties include the sustainability of climate-tech valuation multiples amid macro volatility, capital expenditure requirements specific to frontier-energy infrastructure, and regulatory pathway clarity for the company's core applications. The peer range spread of $2.3B underscores sensitivity to technology differentiation and commercialization risk.
